sections.text:
Modern 6-DoF grasp generators are often evaluated using grasp scores, dataset-level metrics, or single-robot demonstrations, yet proposal quality alone does not determine whether a grasp is executable by a particular robot.

We present GraspBench, a controlled MuJoCo protocol for evaluating complete grasp-generation pipelines after robot-specific inverse-kinematics filtering, motion planning, and fixed approach-close-lift execution.

GraspBench evaluates six configured pipelines across four robot embodiments, five diagnostic objects, and a structured tabletop pose grid, yielding 540 scenarios per method and 3,240 method-scenario evaluations in total.

Missing outputs are conservatively counted as failures, and success follows the binary lift criterion produced by each method's execution runner. GraspGen achieves the highest overall success rate (73.1%), followed by EconomicGrasp (63.5%), while robot- and object-conditioned analyses reveal substantial variation across embodiments and object geometries.

GPG produces the largest native candidate sets but achieves 44.3% success, indicating that proposal volume alone does not guarantee robot-executable grasps. Cluster-aware paired intervals support the principal method differences while not estimating repeated-execution uncertainty.

The results characterize complete configured pipelines on fixed scenarios rather than intrinsic model quality or stochastic repeatability, showing that grasping performance depends jointly on the generator, robot embodiment, scene, and execution protocol.

summary.en: The paper introduces GraspBench, a MuJoCo protocol that evaluates complete 6-DoF grasp-generation pipelines after robot-specific inverse-kinematics filtering, motion planning, and fixed approach-close-lift execution. It compares six configured pipelines across four robot embodiments, five diagnostic objects, and a structured tabletop pose grid. Missing outputs count as failures, and success uses a binary lift criterion. The authors report the highest overall success rate for GraspGen, while GPG produces the largest candidate sets but reaches 44.3% success. Results characterize configured pipelines on fixed scenarios, not intrinsic model quality or stochastic repeatability.

items.title: GraspBench: Execution-Aware Cross-Robot Evaluation of 6-DoF Grasp Generation in MuJoCo

sections.text:
Humanoid locomotion policies trained without an explicit smoothness objective tend to produce jerky, high-energy gaits that stress actuators. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer an appealing reward source: given a rendered rollout, a VLM returns an aesthetic quality score on [0,10] without task-specific feature engineering.

We find, however, that aesthetic preference and physical smoothness point in opposite directions: across four production VLMs, clips with higher joint acceleration receive higher aesthetic scores (mean Pearson r=+0.66).

We study PhySA (Physical Smoothness and Aesthetics), which keeps the two on separate, independently removable reward channels: a sparse, asynchronous VLM score and a phase-triggered correction channel that adjusts physical penalty weights from simulator state. Ablations attribute the smoothness gain to the correction channel.

On MuJoCo Humanoid-v5 at 2.6M steps, PhySA lowers joint acceleration by 26 to 32% relative to vanilla PPO, Text2Reward, and Eureka (three seeds), at the cost of shorter episodes. In a single extended run it lowers joint acceleration by 59.5% relative to Prompt2Policy, while a three-seed replication shows a smaller, non-significant reduction (7.2%).

The gain does not transfer to IsaacLab or the Unitree G1, even after rescaling the smoothness term.

summary.en: The paper studies PhySA, which separates aesthetic and physical rewards for humanoid locomotion into independently removable channels: a sparse asynchronous vision-language score and a phase-triggered correction that adjusts physical penalty weights from simulator state. The authors find that four production VLMs give higher aesthetic scores to clips with greater joint acceleration, and ablations attribute smoothness gains to the correction channel. On MuJoCo Humanoid-v5, a three-seed experiment reports lower acceleration than three baselines at the cost of shorter episodes. An extended single run shows a different-sized gain from a three-seed replication; the gain does not transfer to IsaacLab or Unitree G1.
summary.zh: 论文研究 PhySA，将类人机器人步态的审美奖励与物理平滑奖励分为可独立移除的通道：异步稀疏视觉语言模型评分，以及依据模拟器状态调整物理惩罚权重的相位触发校正。作者发现，四种生产级 VLM 对关节加速度较高的片段给出更高审美分数；消融实验将平滑性提升归因于校正通道。在 MuJoCo Humanoid-v5、260 万步和三随机种子下，PhySA 相对三种基线降低关节加速度，但代价是回合变短。扩展单次运行与三种子复现结果不同；增益未迁移至 IsaacLab 或 Unitree G1。

items.title: PhySA: Decoupling Aesthetic and Physical Rewards for Humanoid Locomotion

sections.text:
Robust motion planning in dense traffic requires autonomous vehicles to interact in rare and safety-critical scenarios that are underrepresented in naturalistic driving data.

Although adversarial training offers a feasible solution, existing methods often rely on external scenario generators, heuristic perturbations, or simulator-heavy rollouts, which makes them difficult to integrate with modern autoregressive planners.

Here, we cast adversarially robust planner learning as a constrained min-max game and propose Adversarial World Modeling (AWM), a theoretically grounded multi-agent self-play fine-tuning framework. Since solving the exact game is intractable, AWM introduces a principled decoupled solver.

In the inner minimization, the planner's predictive world model is converted into a role-conditioned adversary that learns sparse, scene-adaptive attack coalitions via counterfactual credit assignment.

In the outer maximization, the ego planner optimizes a regret-aware robust best response against the frozen AWM, utilizing tail-risk weighting and reference-anchored trust regions to improve hard-case recovery while preserving nominal driving behavior.

Experiments on the nuPlan and InterPlan benchmarks demonstrate that our method generates transferable adversarial interactions and yields a robust planner that achieves competitive closed-loop performance in both nominal and highly interactive long-tail scenarios. Theoretical analysis justifies the decoupled solver and the main optimization components.

summary.en: The paper proposes Adversarial World Modeling (AWM), framing robust motion planning as a constrained min-max game solved through multi-agent self-play fine-tuning. Its inner stage turns the planner’s predictive world model into a role-conditioned adversary that learns sparse, scene-adaptive attack coalitions; the outer stage trains the ego planner against that frozen adversary using tail-risk weighting and reference-anchored trust regions. The authors report competitive closed-loop performance in nominal and interactive long-tail scenarios on nuPlan and InterPlan, alongside theoretical analysis of the solver and optimization components.
summary.zh: 论文提出对抗世界建模（AWM），将鲁棒运动规划表述为受约束的极小极大博弈，并以多智能体自博弈微调求解。内层将规划器的预测世界模型转化为角色条件对手，通过反事实信用分配学习稀疏、适应场景的攻击联盟；外层训练自车规划器，以尾部风险加权和参考锚定信赖域应对冻结的对手。作者报告，nuPlan 与 InterPlan 基准实验显示，该方法可生成可迁移的对抗交互，并在常规及长尾闭环场景中取得有竞争力的表现；理论分析为求解器及优化组件提供依据。

items.title: World Models as Adversaries: Multi-Agent Self-Play Fine-Tuning for Robust Motion Planning

sections.text:
Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage.

These failure modes are invisible from the current state alone, and acting on them requires reasoning about what each candidate action will cause.

World models offer exactly this, namely action-conditioned predictions of the future, but rolling them out at every decision step is a cost deployable navigation systems cannot pay, and the field has largely traded foresight for speed. We argue this is a false dichotomy.

The natural place for a world model in human-aware navigation is at training time, as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast policy, rather than at inference time, as an online planner.

We pair a discrete visual action prior with two task-aligned world models, one for nearby social dynamics and one for future scene semantics, that score candidate actions by their predicted consequences and refine the policy through group-relative preference distillation.

At deployment, both world models are removed and the policy acts in a single forward pass. Across five held-out evaluation scenarios, this yields navigation that is simultaneously safer, more socially and group-coherent, and more goal-directed than strong reactive and learned baselines, with naive observers rating the resulting motion as more human-like.

Taken together, our findings point to a different approach for bringing world-model foresight into deployable agents: not accelerating rollouts, but amortizing them into the policy so that the cost of looking ahead is confined to training. Project page: https://seoneun.github.io/-NeurIPS-2026-Seeing-Beyond-the-Next-Step/

summary.en: The paper argues that world models should serve as preference oracles during training for human-aware navigation, rather than as online planners at deployment. Its method combines a discrete visual action prior with two task-aligned world models, covering nearby social dynamics and future scene semantics. They score candidate actions by predicted consequences and refine the policy through group-relative preference distillation. At deployment, the models are removed and the policy acts in one forward pass. The authors report safer, more coherent, goal-directed, and human-like navigation than baselines across five held-out scenarios.
summary.zh: 论文主张在面向人的导航中，世界模型更适合作为训练阶段的偏好评估器，而非部署时的在线规划器。方法结合离散视觉动作先验，以及分别描述附近社交动态和未来场景语义的两个世界模型；它们依据候选动作的预测后果，通过群体相对偏好蒸馏来改进策略。部署时移除两个世界模型，策略只需一次前向计算。作者报告，在五个留出评估场景中，该方法相较反应式和学习基线更安全、更具群体协调性且更趋向目标，观察者也认为其动作更像人类。

items.title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes

sections.text:
Latent communication enables agents to collaborate efficiently by directly exchanging intermediate model representations rather than raw sensor data or text messages. Existing approaches, however, are primarily designed for LLM agents and do not consider the bandwidth constraints and heterogeneous task deadlines faced by cyber-physical agents.

In this work, we propose SCALE, a real-time latent communication method tailored for cyber-physical agents. Motivated by the spatio-temporal continuity of the physical world, SCALE matches tokens across consecutive latent messages using similarity scores to identify reusable information and avoid redundant transmission.

It then profiles the semantic gain and communication cost of transmitting different amounts of latent information. Based on these profiles, SCALE employs a real-time scheduler that jointly determines which pending messages to transmit and how many latent tokens to send, subject to available bandwidth and task deadlines.

We evaluate SCALE across three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study under diverse network conditions and heterogeneous task deadlines. Our results show that SCALE significantly improves both task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks.

Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SCALE-4E80/.

summary.en: The paper introduces SCALE, a real-time latent communication method for cyber-physical agents facing bandwidth limits and varied task deadlines. It matches tokens across consecutive latent messages by similarity to reuse information and reduce redundant transmission. SCALE also profiles semantic gain and communication cost at different message sizes, then schedules which messages to send and how many tokens to include under bandwidth and deadline constraints. Evaluations across three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study report improved task performance and on-time delivery under diverse network conditions and deadlines.
summary.zh: 论文提出面向信息带宽受限、任务期限各异的网络物理智能体的实时潜在通信方法 SCALE。该方法依据相似度匹配连续潜在消息中的令牌，以复用信息并减少冗余传输；同时评估传输不同数量潜在信息带来的语义收益与通信成本，再由实时调度器在带宽和期限约束下决定待发送消息及令牌数量。作者在三个网络物理基准和一个实体蜘蛛机器人案例中评估该方法，并报告其在多种网络条件和任务期限下提升了任务表现与按时交付。

items.title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents

sections.text:
Defense systems for maritime assets must distinguish approaching benign craft from uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) with sufficient warning to act. Shore cameras using computer vision can separate hostile vessels from benign traffic, but these systems may be attacked using an adversarial hull patch or physical disguise.

We evaluate adversarial hull patches and find they suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign. Physical disguise, however, can bypass both a camera check and a radar presence check.

To evaluate defenses, we develop a hybrid replay protocol from automatic identification system (AIS) tracks that combines recorded benign motion with direct or off-axis attack run-ins.

We find that for recreational-labeled vessels attacking via direct run-in within 4 nautical miles, an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94-95% at 15-20 knots, compared with 12% for a track-only speed check.

The checks are complementary on off-axis approaches, constraining the attacker to remain below both thresholds and extending the time required to reach the asset. Flagging on either check has a 4.9% held-out false-alarm rate overall and 12.3% on recreational traffic.

The replay-based evaluation protocol supports comparative test and evaluation of defense methods.

summary.en: The paper evaluates defenses against disguised uncrewed surface vessels. Adversarial hull patches suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but do not cause benign misclassification; physical disguises can bypass both camera and radar-presence checks. The authors develop an AIS-track replay protocol combining recorded benign motion with direct or off-axis attack approaches. For direct run-ins by recreational-labeled vessels, an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94–95% at 15–20 knots, versus 12% for a track-speed check. The checks complement each other on off-axis approaches; flagging either yields a 4.9% overall held-out false-alarm rate and 12.3% on recreational traffic.

sections.text:
Reinforcement learning (RL) promises to unlock capabilities beyond imitation learning for Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models, but its requirement for massive real-world interaction prevents direct deployment on physical robots.

Recent work attempts to use learned world models as simulators for policy optimization, yet closed-loop imagined rollouts inevitably suffer from hallucination and long-horizon error accumulation. Such errors not only degrade visual fidelity, but also mislead policy optimization by providing unreliable learning signals.

We propose WoVR, a reliable world-model-based RL framework for post-training VLA policies. Instead of assuming a faithful world model, WoVR explicitly regulates how RL interacts with imperfect imagined dynamics.

It improves rollout stability through a controllable action-conditioned video world model, reshapes imagined interaction to reduce effective error depth via Keyframe-Initialized Rollouts, and maintains policy--simulator alignment through World Model-Policy co-evolution.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that WoVR enables stable long-horizon imagined rollouts and effective policy optimization, achieving superior LIBERO performance and consistent real-world gains across multiple robotic platforms. These results show that world models can serve as practical simulators for RL when hallucination is explicitly controlled.

Additional visualization results are available at https://wovr-rlinf.github.io.

summary.en: The paper introduces WoVR, a world-model-based framework for reinforcement-learning post-training of vision-language-action policies. It addresses hallucinations and accumulated errors in imagined rollouts with a controllable action-conditioned video model, keyframe-initialized rollouts, and co-evolution of the policy and world model. The authors report stable long-horizon imagined rollouts, improved policy optimization and LIBERO performance, and consistent gains on real-world tasks across multiple robotic platforms.
summary.zh: 论文提出 WoVR，用世界模型支持视觉—语言—动作（VLA）策略的强化学习后训练，旨在减少真实机器人交互需求，并应对想象轨迹中的幻觉和误差累积。该框架通过可控的动作条件视频世界模型、关键帧初始化轨迹和世界模型—策略协同演化，调节策略与不完美模拟器的交互。作者报告，实验中该方法实现了稳定的长时程想象轨迹、较好的 LIBERO 表现，并在多个机器人平台上取得一致的真实场景增益。

items.title: WoVR: World Models as Reliable Simulators for Post-Training VLA Policies with RL

sections.text:
This paper presents a robotic harvesting method that combines RGB-D fruit localization, GA-based harvest ordering, and waypoint-based robot motion in dense and unstructured crop environments. The global RGB-D camera provides 3D fruit positions for ordering, while the end-effector-mounted camera provides close-range observation during execution.

The GA determines the harvesting sequence, and static or dynamic waypoints define the intermediate robot motion. The method was evaluated in a controlled laboratory testbed and in four-, five-, and six-fruit field conditions. GA solutions were compared with exhaustive enumeration, and both waypoint offsets were examined by parameter sensitivity analysis.

Continuous execution reduced unnecessary Home-return motion, while the dynamic waypoint changed with the remaining fruit distribution without changing the GA sequence.

In the field evaluation, the dynamic-waypoint continuous strategy produced 40 collision events and a 70.7% target-approach success rate, compared with 55 collision events and 65.3% for the static-waypoint continuous strategy.

summary.en: The paper describes a robotic harvesting method for dense, unstructured crop environments, combining RGB-D fruit localization, genetic-algorithm harvest ordering, and waypoint-based motion. A global camera supplies fruit positions, while an end-effector camera provides close-range observation during execution. Evaluation covered a controlled laboratory testbed and field conditions with four to six fruits. In the field evaluation, the dynamic-waypoint continuous strategy had 40 collision events and a 70.7% target-approach success rate, compared with 55 events and 65.3% for the static-waypoint strategy.

sections.text:
For perceptive humanoid locomotion, the relevance of terrain geometry depends on the robot's body state and how both evolve under its actions. Existing work has advanced terrain-aware sensory fusion and cross-modal prediction, improving how visual and proprioceptive information is combined and related.

However, feature aggregation alone does not specify which cross-modal relationships should be learned, while prediction between simultaneous observations does not explicitly constrain their action-dependent evolution.

We present Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction (STEP), a one-stage framework that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution within a shared control representation. Multiple learned queries aggregate depth and proprioceptive tokens into a compact policy state.

Bidirectional masked prediction uses each visible modality to predict latent features of the omitted modality, explicitly supervising terrain-body relationships.

An action-conditioned predictor maps the current policy state and executed action to the next fused state, with an exponential-moving-average target defined directly in the policy representation space.

Simulation comparisons show overall improvements in terrain traversal over evaluated fusion alternatives and ablations, while depth-dropout and delay experiments demonstrate the benefits of both predictive objectives under degraded visual input.

Deployed on a 23-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid with onboard sensing, STEP succeeds in 98 of 100 hardware trials across stairs, a 40\,cm platform, a 70\,cm gap, stepping stones, and backward stair traversal without rearward terrain visibility.

summary.en: The paper presents STEP, a one-stage training framework for perceptive humanoid locomotion that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution. Learned queries combine depth and proprioceptive tokens into a policy state; bidirectional masked prediction and an action-conditioned next-state predictor provide explicit training objectives. Simulation comparisons show improved terrain traversal over evaluated fusion alternatives and ablations, while depth-dropout and delay experiments indicate benefits under degraded visual input. The authors report 98 successful trials out of 100 on a 23-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid across several terrains.

sections.text:
Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion.

However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding.

VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories.

Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement.

It trains on annotated primitives and accepts structurally valid predictions without requiring target-token agreement. In evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, the authors report consistently lower prediction errors than autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate about 25x faster generation for 3D point-motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, versus 62.6% for the baseline.

sections.text:
VREgo trains manipulation policies from demonstrations recorded on consumer VR headsets; we instantiate it with EgoKit on one such headset, the PICO 4 Ultra. On-device head and hand tracking and stereo object localisation allow the operator to begin a demonstration at the table.

We adapt HumanEgo's preprocessing to estimate grasp thresholds per recording, update object positions after release, and propagate segmentation masks between keyframes. We evaluate policies in simulation on two tabletop tasks recorded by one operator. For cube placement, we compare PICO and Project Aria recordings of the same 41 layouts.

With 40 training demonstrations, the PICO policies placed the cube on the tray in 67, 74, and 60 of 100 evaluation layouts across three training seeds. The corresponding Aria results were 73, 78, and 0.

For a two-stage stacking task recorded with the PICO alone, the baseline placed the block on the tray in 94 of 100 layouts and met the end-of-episode criterion for both placements in two. In one diagnostic episode, repeated replanning deferred release beyond the eight executed steps.

Demonstration replays also showed that the open gripper could displace the cube before grasping it. After adapting the training trajectories and adding task-specific execution rules that use simulator object positions, the system met both placement criteria in 93.8% of episodes across four evaluation noise seeds.

The same 100 layouts informed rule development and evaluation. VREgo is available at https://vrego.chuange.org/.

summary.en: VREgo trains manipulation policies from egocentric demonstrations recorded with consumer VR headsets, instantiated with EgoKit on a PICO 4 Ultra. Policies were evaluated in simulation on two tabletop tasks recorded by one operator. For cube placement, PICO and Project Aria recordings were compared on the same 41 layouts, using 40 demonstrations; results varied across three training seeds. In the two-stage stacking task, the PICO baseline met both placement criteria in only two of 100 layouts. After adapting trajectories and adding task-specific rules using simulator object positions, the system met both criteria in 93.8% of episodes across four evaluation noise seeds. The same 100 layouts were used for rule development and evaluation.

sections.text:
Wheeled humanoid robots carry both arms on one actuated waist, usually without torque sensors, so the accuracy of both end-effectors depends on a single waist model. After a first stage that estimates the tracker and target extrinsics, we identify the waist and both arms in one problem from the target positions on both flanges, measured by an optical tracker.

The kinematic model is complete, with waist-base, parallel-axis, and branch parameters; arm compliances are driven by measured torques and waist compliances by gravity torques of the robot's mass model; and Gaussian priors with evidence-maximizing scales stabilize the estimate.

Independent and sequential single-chain calibration are restrictions of this problem, and its waist information is the sum of the single-chain Schur complements. On two robots with different waists, each without and with a payload, calibration reduces the mean errors on held-out poses from 11.3-31.1 mm to 0.50-1.11 mm.

For every training-set size from 20 poses to all, the method has 17-63% lower mean errors than adaptations of two published whole-body calibration methods, mainly through the waist compliance. Independent calibration yields two waist models; using either for both arms raises the other arm's error to up to 3.21 mm.

summary.en: The paper proposes whole-body calibration for wheeled humanoid robots using a shared-waist dual-chain model that jointly estimates waist and arm parameters from optically tracked target positions on both flanges. The model includes waist and branch geometry, arm compliance driven by measured torques, waist compliance driven by gravity torques, and Gaussian priors with evidence-maximizing scales. On two robots with different waists, tested without and with payloads, mean errors on held-out poses fell from 11.3–31.1 mm to 0.50–1.11 mm. Across training set sizes from 20 poses to all poses, mean errors were 17–63% lower than adaptations of two published whole-body calibration methods, mainly through waist compliance.

sections.text:
Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. This separation limits how much pretrained perception and reasoning can guide action generation, especially in out-of-distribution settings.

We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions.

At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control.

Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency.

On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated $\pi_{0.5}$-based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale.

It also improves performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and raises the average success rate across four real-world bimanual tasks by 20.8 percentage points compared with $\pi_{0.5}$.

summary.en: The paper introduces JADE, a framework in which a vision-language model and an action expert jointly denoise robot actions. At each step, the vision-language model reads the noisy action alongside visual observations and language instructions, then guides the expert through gated cross-attention. Training also teaches it to recover clean action latents. The authors say joint denoising can reduce sampling steps, with adaptive step sizes balancing performance and latency. Evaluations cover RoboDojo, RoboTwin 2.0, and four real-world bimanual tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 JADE，一种让视觉语言模型与动作专家共同去噪的机器人动作生成框架。每一步中，视觉语言模型读取带噪动作、图像和语言指令，并通过门控交叉注意力引导动作专家；训练还监督其从带噪潜变量恢复干净动作。作者称该方法可减少采样步数，并以自适应步长权衡性能和延迟。在 RoboDojo、RoboTwin 2.0 及四项真实双手机器人任务的评估中，论文报告了相应性能提升。

items.title: Vision-Language Models Are Joint Denoisers in Robotic Action Generation

sections.text:
Translating language into humanoid motion requires coordinating body parts, determining motion duration, and producing references suitable for robot execution. We introduce PartiGen, a part-aware latent diffusion framework that incorporates anatomical structure into a shared whole-body motion representation.

Part-specific attention processes anatomically masked frame features, and its outputs are fused to combine local limb information with whole-body context. Conditioned on text and motion history, the model generates motion primitives autoregressively.

Forward-kinematics supervision encourages kinematic consistency, while a learned end-of-sequence predictor selects a frame-level endpoint after generation. On HumanML3D retargeted to the Unitree G1, PartiGen achieves a segment-level FID of 3.165, a 16.8% reduction over TextOp, and improves R@1 by 1.4 percentage points.

In the duration study with 16-frame primitives, endpoint prediction reduces mean absolute duration error from 12.471 to 3.080 frames compared with a fixed-length cutoff. We further evaluate robot execution using a pretrained, frozen GRIT tracker: 409 of 500 generated references (81.8%) pass the posture-based stability screen in MuJoCo.

Following simulation screening and manual selection, 26 of 27 attempted motions are judged successful on the real G1.

summary.en: The paper presents PartiGen, a part-aware latent diffusion framework that incorporates anatomy into a whole-body motion representation and generates motion primitives autoregressively from text and motion history. It uses part-specific attention, forward-kinematics supervision, and a learned endpoint predictor. On HumanML3D retargeted to Unitree G1, the authors report improved segment-level FID and R@1; a duration study reports lower error with endpoint prediction. Robot execution is evaluated with a frozen GRIT tracker, simulation screening in MuJoCo, and manual selection, followed by real G1 attempts.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PartiGen，一种将人体解剖结构融入全身动作表示的部件感知潜变量扩散框架，可依据文本和动作历史自回归生成动作片段。模型使用部件特定注意力、正向运动学监督和学习得到的终止帧预测器。在 HumanML3D 重定向至 Unitree G1 的评估中，作者报告片段级 FID 和 R@1 改善；时长研究显示终点预测降低了时长误差。机器人执行评估使用冻结的 GRIT 跟踪器，并经过 MuJoCo 稳定性筛选和人工挑选；论文报告真实 G1 尝试中多数动作成功。

sections.text:
Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation.

Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training.

Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes.

To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations.

Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.

summary.en: The paper introduces SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action model that extends implicit spatial alignment through continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, it jointly trains action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. The authors unify diverse robot datasets and use feature-dependent gates to aggregate visual features. A teacher uses partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB. Probabilistic state dropout encourages visual reliance; auxiliary components are training-only, preserving the original inference architecture.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SLA，通过持续预训练扩展空间语言动作模型的隐式空间对齐能力，并在下游后训练中保持该能力。模型从预训练 pi05 策略初始化，联合优化动作预测，以及中间视觉嵌入与冻结三维感知模型空间表示的对齐。作者整理多样化机器人数据集，并设计依赖特征的门控来聚合多层视觉嵌入；教师模型结合部分可用的深度、相机标定和 RGB 数据进行监督。概率状态丢弃用于鼓励模型依赖视觉线索。辅助组件仅用于训练，推理时保留原有架构。

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people.

Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements.

We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead.

We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines.

Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success.

We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.

summary.en: The paper presents VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over latent layers of a vision-language-action model for timely failure detection, bounded missed-detection and false-alarm rates, and failure-mode prediction. The authors report that training on pre-failure trajectory segments improves early detection at matched false-positive rates. Under shifts to unseen tasks, the rate bounds remain valid in many runs. The probe also improves top-three failure-mode accuracy over a majority baseline. The authors say real-time monitoring can support lightweight steering that improves task success, and describe an annotated manipulation-episode dataset.
summary.zh: 论文提出 VLA-Tug，一种针对视觉语言动作模型潜层的轻量探针，用于及时检测失败、控制漏报与误报，并预测失败类型。作者报告，在相同假阳性率下，使用轨迹失败前片段监督可提升早期检测表现；面对未见任务时，漏报和误报率界限在多数运行中仍有效。该方法在未见任务上的前三名失败类型准确率也高于多数类基线。论文称实时探针可支持轻量引导并改善任务成功率，并发布了标注的操作轨迹数据集。

sections.text:
Distance based formation control fixes the shape of a robot team but leaves its position and orientation unconstrained. We regulate all three for differential drive robots that have only one absolute position anchor, absolute headings, body frame relative position measurements, and communication with their neighbors.

We derive a two layer estimation control scheme directly from optimization. The first half of the result is a set of graph-proximal estimators that reconstruct the centroid, the anchor vector, and the centered coordinates.

Exact proximal updates reach consensus in finitely many steps, and a finite number of primal dual iterations leaves a bounded reconstruction error. The controller combines proximal centroid and orientation steps with distance gradient shape regulation, and a finite rotation removes the orientation drift caused by the shape step.

A discrete Lyapunov analysis gives local exponential convergence once the estimators have converged. We validate the method in ROS 2 Gazebo and in experiments with five physical robots.

summary.en: The paper presents an optimization-derived, two-layer estimation and control scheme for differential-drive formations with one absolute position anchor, absolute headings, body-frame relative-position measurements, and neighbor communication. Graph-proximal estimators reconstruct the centroid, anchor vector, and centered coordinates; the controller combines centroid and orientation regulation with distance-based shape control and a finite rotation to compensate orientation drift. The authors report finite-step consensus for exact updates, bounded reconstruction error after finitely many primal-dual iterations, and local exponential convergence after estimator convergence. Validation includes ROS 2 Gazebo and experiments with five physical robots.
summary.zh: 本文针对仅有一个绝对位置锚点、绝对航向、机体坐标系相对位置测量及邻居通信的差速机器人编队，提出由优化推导的两层估计与控制方法。图近端估计器重建质心、锚点向量和中心化坐标；控制器结合质心与朝向调节、距离梯度形状控制及有限旋转补偿。作者称，精确更新可有限步达成一致，有限次原始—对偶迭代产生有界重建误差；估计器收敛后，局部指数收敛由离散李雅普诺夫分析给出。方法在 ROS 2 Gazebo 仿真及五台实体机器人实验中验证。

sections.text:
Robot foundation models have shown remarkable performance in robot control, yet adapting them to a new task still relies heavily on teleoperated demonstrations.

Egocentric human videos offer a scalable substitute, but overlaying rendered robots on human videos or retargeting human poses into robot actions leaves significant visual or action gaps for high-DoF robot embodiments.

To address this limitation, we propose RoboTryOn, which treats human-to-robot translation as virtual try-on: try-on keeps the person and swaps the garment, RoboTryOn keeps the demonstrated motion and swaps the human for the robot.

Specifically, RoboTryOn converts a human video into a video of the target robot specified by a reference image, while preserving the original task, objects, and background. To maintain visual consistency, we translate selected keyframes autoregressively and use them to guide video synthesis with motion conditioned on the human hand skeleton.

Additionally, we use an inverse dynamics model (IDM) that incorporates depth features to infer action labels from synthesized videos for policy learning.

Our experiments across multiple humanoid embodiments show that policies trained with our synthetic data improve the average success rate on novel tasks, including challenging bimanual manipulation, from 2% to 60%, without any real robot demonstration of those tasks.

Moreover, training with our synthetic data matches the performance of policies trained solely on teleoperated demonstrations at approximately a third of the collection cost, demonstrating the cost efficiency of our approach.

summary.en: The paper proposes RoboTryOn, which converts egocentric human videos into videos of a target robot specified by a reference image while preserving the demonstrated motion, task objects, and background. Selected keyframes are translated autoregressively and guide video synthesis conditioned on the human hand skeleton. An inverse dynamics model using depth features infers action labels from synthesized videos for policy learning. In experiments across multiple humanoid embodiments, the authors report that synthetic-data-trained policies raise average success on novel tasks, including bimanual manipulation, from 2% to 60% without real robot demonstrations of those tasks. They also report matching teleoperation-trained policy performance at about one-third of the collection cost.
summary.zh: 本文提出 RoboTryOn，将人类第一视角视频转换为由参考图像指定的目标机器人视频，同时保留演示动作、任务物体和背景。方法以自回归方式转换选定关键帧，并利用人体手部骨架动作条件指导视频合成；随后通过结合深度特征的逆动力学模型，从合成视频推断动作标签以训练策略。作者报告，在多个类人机器人形态的实验中，合成数据训练的策略在新任务上的平均成功率从 2% 提升至 60%，包括双手操作任务，且无需这些任务的真实机器人演示。其成本约为遥操作演示数据采集的三分之一，并达到相当表现。

sections.text:
Legged robots equipped with manipulators have shown significant potential in the fields of daily life and industry in complex environments.

However, existing methods mainly focus on global navigation or manipulation independently, while overlooking the last-mile navigation problem, where the robot must jointly determine the base placement, approach direction, and grasp execution to achieve reliable object grasping, and different manipulation stages require distinct control behaviors.

To address these challenges, we propose Last-Mile Grasp-Navigation (LMGN), a unified policy learning model for Quadruped robot loco-manipulation. An Explicit Distance and Directional Reachability (ED-DR) representation is first introduced to explicitly represent the features of grasp-compatible base placement and approach direction.

We then develop a semantically aligned Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts (HMoE) policy that models stage-aware behaviors across the stages of base adjustment, pre-grasp alignment and grasp execution, and object lift.

Finally, a new optimization method that jointly aligns navigation and manipulation, stage-dependent expert routing, and action-level consistency is proposed to optimize the HMoE policy.

Extensive experiments on the Habitat and Isaac Gym simulators demonstrate that LMGN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, denoting that integrating grasp-aware reachability with stage-aware policy learning significantly improves the success rates of last-mile navigation and target grasp for robots.

summary.en: The paper proposes LMGN, a unified policy-learning model for quadruped robot locomotion and manipulation that jointly addresses base placement, approach direction, and grasp execution. A joint optimization method aligns navigation and manipulation, stage-dependent expert routing, and action-level consistency. The authors report that experiments in the Habitat and Isaac Gym simulators show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods in last-mile navigation and target-grasp success.

Social touch interactions, such as handshakes, fist bumps, and hugs, require humanoid robots to infer human intent, generate contact-rich motions, and maintain safe physical contact. We present AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pipeline deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands.

A lightweight RGB-based model recognizes interaction intent from two onboard cameras and converts it into a language prompt for the VLA policy. Low-confidence predictions suppress motion execution, reducing unintended activations.

During physical contact, interaction-specific compliance profiles adjust arm impedance, while an independent voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe-stop procedure. Using VR teleoperation, we collected approximately 1,300 multimodal interaction episodes and fine-tuned four VLA models: GR00T, RLDX-1, Being-H0.5, and UnifoLM-VLA-0.

On-robot evaluation identifies GR00T as the best-performing standalone model. Integrating intent recognition increases its macro-F1 score from 0.75 to 0.90, while the intent model achieves a p95 inference latency of 6.27 ms.

These results demonstrate that explicit intent gating improves the reliability of VLA-based social interaction without compromising real-time operation.

summary.en: The paper presents AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated vision-language-action pipeline for social touch, deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid. A lightweight RGB model uses two onboard cameras to infer interaction intent and prompt the VLA policy; low-confidence predictions suppress motion. Interaction-specific compliance adjusts arm impedance during contact, and a separate voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe stop. The authors collected approximately 1,300 multimodal episodes through VR teleoperation and fine-tuned four VLA models. On-robot evaluation found GR00T the strongest standalone model. Intent recognition raised its macro-F1 from 0.75 to 0.90, with 6.27 ms p95 inference latency.

sections.text:
Physical human--robot interaction requires controllers capable of maintaining intrinsically bounded interactions with the environment. The Fractal Impedance Controller (FIC) has been proven to guarantee these safety characteristics by design.

This paper introduces the robotic implementation and experimental validation of its most advanced architecture: the Harmonic-Passive Motion Paradigm (H-PMP), an evolution of the Passive Motion Paradigm designed to mimic human-like interaction.

Furthermore, we present a unified framework for FIC deployment, supported by an open-source software suite featuring ROS2, MuJoCo, and physical hardware integrations.

Through three experiments conducted on a Kinova Gen3 arm (trajectory tracking, a wall press with sudden loss of contact, and learning-by-demonstration) we compare the H-PMP against earlier FIC architectures. The results demonstrate that the H-PMP achieves a seamless trade-off between admittance and impedance behaviours.

This makes it ideal for deployment in unstructured environments, enabling the robot to transition between interaction modes with no computational overhead.

summary.en: The paper presents a unified deployment framework for the Fractal Impedance Controller (FIC) and the robotic implementation and experimental validation of its Harmonic-Passive Motion Paradigm (H-PMP), designed to support human-like interaction. An open-source suite integrates ROS2, MuJoCo, and physical hardware. Three experiments on a Kinova Gen3 arm compare H-PMP with earlier FIC architectures: trajectory tracking, wall pressing after sudden contact loss, and learning by demonstration. The authors report a seamless trade-off between admittance and impedance behavior and transitions between interaction modes without computational overhead.

sections.text:
Cooperative localization uses odometry and inter-robot measurements to estimate the motion of a robot team. These measurements describe only relative geometry, but the team's estimated position and orientation can drift together over time, i.e., gauge drift.

In this work, we study correction of this gauge drift using a radio attenuation map registered in the same world coordinate frame used for robot poses. Specifically, we propose Radio-to-Pose Information (RPI), an interface that converts power residuals and their pose derivatives into a Gaussian information matrix and vector pair.

RPI builds on the insight that received power is sensitive to shared displacement in the world map. The pose estimator uses the interface together with odometry and inter-robot measurements to update poses and minimize uncertainty. We characterize the shared motions detectable from the map and observed links.

For an uncertain shared map, RPI keeps correlations across robots and time and reproduces joint Gaussian pose estimates and covariances. Across $1000$ simulated Gaussian trials, RPI matches the results of joint estimation.

Across 32 paired trials with a registered map, RPI reduces common-position RMSE from $0.542$m to $0.140$m in a $50\times50$m arena compared with a baseline that uses radio only to weight relative measurements.

summary.en: The work studies correction of team-wide pose drift in cooperative localization using a radio attenuation map registered to the robots’ world coordinate frame. The proposed Radio-to-Pose Information (RPI) interface converts power residuals and their pose derivatives into a Gaussian information matrix and vector for the pose estimator to use alongside odometry and inter-robot measurements. For an uncertain shared map, RPI preserves correlations across robots and time. In 1,000 simulated Gaussian trials it matches joint estimation. In 32 paired trials with a registered map, common-position RMSE fell from 0.542 m to 0.140 m in a 50 × 50 m arena versus a baseline that used radio only to weight relative measurements.
summary.zh: 本文研究利用与机器人位姿处于同一世界坐标系的无线电衰减图，校正协作定位中的整体位姿漂移。作者提出无线电到位姿信息（RPI）接口，将功率残差及其位姿导数转换为高斯信息矩阵和向量，供位姿估计器结合里程计和机器人间测量更新位姿、降低不确定性。对于不确定的共享地图，RPI保留机器人之间及时间上的相关性。1000次模拟高斯试验中，RPI与联合估计结果一致；32组配对试验显示，在50×50米场地中，相比仅用无线电加权相对测量的基线，共同位置RMSE由0.542米降至0.140米。

items.title: Radio-to-Pose Information for Gauge-Drift Correction in Cooperative Localization

sections.text:
Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC).We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control.

The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions.

RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently.

The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost.

Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks.

Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%.Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

summary.en: RoboARCade is a benchmark for agentic robot control, with long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments to assess in-context adaptation, memory, reasoning, and precise control. Tasks extend open-source benchmarks by broadening initial conditions, run on MuJoCo, and use interchangeable interfaces. Reported scores are 49.8% for GPT-6 Astra and 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1. A richer visual interface adds 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures mostly involve strategy choice or imprecise execution. On a five-task subset, demonstrations or self-revised prompts improve Astra’s reported performance.
summary.zh: RoboARCade是面向智能体机器人控制的基准，包含三种机器人形态上的长时程操作任务，用于测试上下文适应、记忆、推理和精确控制。任务基于开源基准并扩大初始条件范围，统一运行于MuJoCo，支持可互换接口。基准结果显示，GPT-6 Astra得分49.8%，Claude Fable 5.1得分43.6%；更丰富的视觉接口仅提升1.5至6.8个百分点，但成本为1.7至2.3倍。失败多源于策略选择或执行精度问题。摘要还报告，在五任务子集中，一次成功示范或智能体自行编写并修订提示词可提升表现；这些结果限于所述基准及子集。

sections.text:
Heterogeneous multi-robot collaboration over long horizons requires both global task planning and robust coordination during execution.

Existing plan- ners using large language models (LLMs) can generate task decompositions or symbolic plans, but often execute them as rigid action sequences, making them fragile to local state mismatches and synchronization failures. We propose Em- boTeam, a neuro-symbolic framework for asymmetric state grounding.

An LLM generates structured state expectations, which are verified and coordinated through symbolic search using Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) and then grounded into a team-level parallel behavior tree.

Robot-specific subtrees per- form precondition checking, skill execution, effect validation, local replanning, and blackboard-based synchronization. We further introduce MACE-THOR, con- taining 42 heterogeneous multi-robot tasks across 8 indoor layouts.

EmboTeam improves task success rate from 12% to 55% and goal condition recall from 32% to 75% over LaMMA-P, demonstrating the effectiveness of synchronized reactive grounding for collaboration over long horizons.

summary.en: The paper proposes EmboTeam, a neuro-symbolic framework for long-horizon collaboration among heterogeneous robots, addressing the fragility of rigid action sequences when local states mismatch or synchronization fails. An LLM generates structured state expectations, which PDDL symbolic search verifies and coordinates before grounding them in a team-level parallel behavior tree. Robot-specific subtrees check preconditions, execute skills, validate effects, replan locally, and synchronize through a blackboard. The authors introduce MACE-THOR, with 42 heterogeneous multi-robot tasks across 8 indoor layouts. Compared with LaMMA-P, EmboTeam raises task success from 12% to 55% and goal-condition recall from 32% to 75%.
summary.zh: 本文提出EmboTeam，一种用于异构多机器人长时程协作的神经符号框架，针对刚性动作序列容易受局部状态不匹配和同步失败影响的问题。大语言模型生成结构化状态预期，随后通过PDDL符号搜索验证和协调，并形成团队级并行行为树。各机器人子树执行前置条件检查、技能执行、效果验证、局部重规划及基于黑板的同步。作者还介绍包含8种室内布局、42项异构多机器人任务的MACE-THOR。与LaMMA-P相比，EmboTeam的任务成功率从12%提高至55%，目标条件召回率从32%提高至75%。

items.title: EmboTeam: Asymmetric State Grounding for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Collaboration

sections.text:
We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold.

First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force.

Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text.

We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments.

We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments.

Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, and our readout circuitry enables high dynamic range (HDR) acquisition, measuring, for example, a 3.7 kg weight stack and a 20 g weight on the same sensor in the same frame. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos at opentac.github.io

summary.en: The paper introduces OpenTac, a customizable resistive tactile skin and supporting ecosystem. A structured deformable overlay converts tangential loading into spatial pressure variation; differences between neighboring taxels encode local shear vectors, while common-mode response encodes normal force. The ecosystem includes a design tool that generates fabrication files from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, a simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and adaptive acquisition. The authors report fabricating sensors for varied robot embodiments and demonstrate tactile sensing in real-world control and manipulation policy learning.
summary.zh: 论文提出 OpenTac，一套可定制、可扩展的电阻式触觉皮肤及配套生态。其结构化可变形覆盖层将切向载荷转化为空间压力差，邻近触觉单元的差分响应用于解码剪切方向，整体响应表示法向力。系统还包括可从二维轮廓和可展开三维表面生成制造文件的设计工具、传感器模拟器、跨传感器迁移及自适应采集。作者报告在多种机器人上设计制作传感器，并展示三维触觉在真实机器人控制与策略学习中的应用。

sections.text:
Teleoperation is a key interface for controlling dexterous robotic hands and collecting demonstrations for imitation learning. Its effectiveness largely depends on kinematic retargeting, which maps operator hand motions to feasible and intuitive robot hand motions.

Existing methods often require hand-crafted objectives, precise calibration, or global shape matching between human and robot hand spaces, making them sensitive to hand-specific tuning and less reliable across different dexterous hands.

We propose AnyDexRT, a calibration-efficient retargeting method for intuitive dexterous teleoperation across human-like dexterous hands. AnyDexRT combines self-supervised fingertip correspondence learning with few-shot human guidance to anchor the mapping in task-relevant regions, and further refines pinch-related poses using a contact classifier.

Experiments on diverse dexterous hands and real-world teleoperation tasks show that AnyDexRT improves retargeting quality, reduces manual tuning, and provides more intuitive and efficient control than prior retargeting methods. Project website: https://chenxi-wang.github.io/projects/anydexrt

summary.en: The paper presents AnyDexRT, a method for mapping human hand motion to feasible dexterous-robot-hand motion for teleoperation and demonstration collection. It combines self-supervised fingertip correspondence learning with few-shot human guidance to anchor mappings in task-relevant regions, then refines pinch-related poses using a contact classifier. Experiments across diverse dexterous hands and real-world teleoperation tasks show, according to the authors, improved retargeting quality, less manual tuning, and more intuitive and efficient control than prior methods.

sections.text:
Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint.

This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints.

Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented.

We present MOMASPLAT, a novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions.

Our key insight is that standard MoMa data collection naturally provides the multiview observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D.

MOMASPLAT combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to separately reconstruct the scene and manipulated object, render them from novel viewpoints, and generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations paired with transformed actions.

We evaluate MOMASPLAT on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation.

MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.

summary.en: The paper introduces MOMASPLAT, which augments mobile manipulation demonstrations with full trajectories from unseen robot base viewpoints, including dynamic object interactions after contact. It combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to reconstruct the scene and manipulated object and produce synthetic demonstrations with transformed actions. The authors evaluate five real-world tasks across three scenes and validate demonstration fidelity against ground truth in simulation. They report improved robustness to unseen base poses and reduced need for large-scale real-world data collection.
summary.zh: 论文提出MOMASPLAT，用于为移动操作模仿学习示范生成未见机器人底盘视角下的完整操作轨迹，包括接触后的动态物体交互。方法结合三维高斯泼溅、前馈三维基础模型和基于运动学的动作重定向，分别重建场景与被操作物体，并生成配对变换动作的合成示范。作者在三个场景的五项真实移动操作任务中评估，并在仿真中对照真实值验证示范保真度；报告称其提高了对未见底盘位姿的鲁棒性，且减少大规模真实数据采集需求。

sections.text:
Real-world environments are messy, with paths often blocked by everyday objects like chairs and toys, requiring robots to perform interactive navigation by manipulating obstacles to clear a path. Existing methods rely on extensive simulation-based learning or per-scene instructions specifying which objects to avoid or manipulate.

They struggle to generalize across novel objects, diverse environments, and varied contexts such as a cart of fragile glassware that should be avoided while an empty one can be pushed. We formalize this problem as open-world interactive navigation and present MessyNav, a zero-shot framework based on vision-language models (VLMs).

At its core, MessyNav performs explicit VLM-based affordance reasoning before task planning to decide whether to swipe, pick up, or avoid an object and produce a high-level plan.

Evaluated on a mobile manipulator across real-world indoor and outdoor environments, MessyNav improves success rate by 27 percentage points (pp) over the strongest baseline in real-robot trials and achieves statistically significant gains in a larger-scale offline evaluation, without task-specific training.

summary.en: The paper formalizes navigation through clutter as open-world interactive navigation and presents MessyNav, a framework that requires no task-specific training. It uses vision-language-model-based affordance reasoning before planning to decide whether an obstacle should be swiped, picked up, or avoided, then produces a high-level plan. The authors evaluate it on a mobile manipulator in real indoor and outdoor environments. They report a 27 percentage-point success-rate improvement over the strongest baseline in real-robot trials and statistically significant gains in a larger offline evaluation.

sections.text:
Replay attacks are difficult to detect in vision-based control systems because previously recorded observations can remain plausible while the physical system follows a different trajectory. This paper develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework for detecting replay attacks against vision-based controllers.

A private Gaussian watermark is added to the nominal control input, and a control input-conditioned latent dynamics network (LDN) predicts the corresponding evolution in a compact latent space learned from image observations.

Attack evidence is obtained from the discrepancy between the predicted latent response and the latent representation of the received image observation. A reinforcement learning policy adjusts the watermark covariance using the latent state and detector confidence, thereby balancing attack detectability, watermark energy, and control distortion.

A Lagrangian penalty on task-specific safety costs is included during training to limit the adverse effect of the excitation. The framework is evaluated on a vision-guided UR5 manipulation task in which the robot reaches a target while avoiding a moving human arm under nominal and replay-attacked observations.

summary.en: The paper develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework for detecting replay attacks against vision-based controllers. It adds a private Gaussian watermark to the control input and uses an action-conditioned latent dynamics network to predict the latent response to image observations. Discrepancies provide attack evidence, while a reinforcement learning policy adjusts watermark covariance to balance detectability, energy, and control distortion. Training includes a Lagrangian penalty on task-specific safety costs. Evaluation is in a vision-guided UR5 manipulation task involving a target and a moving human arm.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种用于视觉控制器的自适应动态水印框架，以检测重放攻击。框架在控制输入中加入私有高斯水印，并用动作条件潜在动力学网络预测图像观测的潜在响应，通过预测与接收观测的差异获取攻击证据。强化学习策略根据潜在状态和检测置信度调整水印协方差，以权衡可检测性、水印能量和控制失真；训练中加入任务安全成本的拉格朗日惩罚。评估限于视觉引导的 UR5 操作任务，包括避开移动人臂并接近目标。

sections.text:
Robotic simulators that represent shear within tactile sensing are becoming increasingly important for contact-rich manipulation. However, simulating contact shear with high-fidelity deformable or soft-body simulation is computationally demanding, limiting scalability to large-scale reinforcement learning.

Here we introduce \textit{TactileLab}, a scalable multimodal tactile simulation framework built on IsaacLab, with a particular focus on a new optical-flow-based tactile representation termed \textit{simulated tactile flow}.

Instead of relying on soft-body physics to model shear deformation, TactileLab uses rigid-body simulation to efficiently estimate dense tangential motion at the contact interface, producing tactile flow fields that encode shear-relevant contact dynamics. This flow field complements geometric features from a contact depth field.

We further introduce a novel policy architecture for jointly processing long-horizon proprioceptive signals and rich tactile observations. Across multiple contact-rich tasks, policies trained using simulated tactile flow learn efficiently at scale and exhibit emergent contact-aware behaviours.

To facilitate sim-to-real policy deployment, we then propose a novel real-to-sim tactile translation method that maps real tactile image streams to simulated tactile flow and depth fields, together with a new tactile data collection method, and validate it across diverse tactile sensor designs.

Using this pipeline, we demonstrate real-world deployment on tasks encompassing dual-arm and dexterous in-hand manipulation. Overall, TactileLab provides an end-to-end sim-to-real framework for scalable tactile policy learning, enabling diverse shear-sensitive manipulation across heterogeneous tactile robotic systems.

summary.en: The paper introduces TactileLab, a multimodal tactile simulation framework built on IsaacLab, with an optical-flow-based representation called simulated tactile flow. Rigid-body simulation estimates tangential motion at contact, complementing geometric features from depth fields. The authors report efficient large-scale policy learning and emergent contact-aware behaviors across multiple contact-rich tasks. They also propose translating real tactile images into simulated flow and depth fields, and describe validation across sensor designs and real-world dual-arm and dexterous in-hand manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TactileLab，一种基于 IsaacLab 的多模态触觉仿真框架，重点是用光流表示触觉剪切。它以刚体仿真估计接触界面的切向运动，生成与接触深度场几何特征互补的触觉流场，并提出联合处理长时本体感觉信号和触觉观测的策略架构。作者称，在多种接触丰富任务中，策略可高效规模化学习并表现出接触感知行为。论文还提出将真实触觉图像转换为模拟触觉流与深度场的方法，并在多种传感器设计及双臂和灵巧手真实操作任务中验证部署流程。

items.title: TactileLab: Sim-to-Real Dexterous Robot Manipulation with Efficient Shear-Sensitive Tactile Simulation

sections.text:
Egocentric video is increasingly used as a data source for robot learning, activity understanding, and embodied AI research, but collecting it at scale remains fragmented in practice: each candidate host device, such as an Android phone, iPhone, iPad, smart glasses, or extended reality (XR) headset, exposes a different SDK, a different policy on raw camera access, and different limitations on external USB cameras and on-device tracking.

Synchronized ego-view and wrist-view capture is therefore typically obtained by either committing to a single proprietary platform or building one-off rigs that do not transfer across devices. To address this gap, we present EgoKit, a toolkit that exposes the same egocentric recording workflow across six heterogeneous host devices.

Across all supported devices, EgoKit presents the same recording interaction and produces locally stored video with a uniform log format; on XR headsets, it additionally logs head pose and OpenXR-standard 26-joint hand tracking aligned to the video streams.

The companion accessories, including two wrist cameras with mounts, a head strap, and a USB-C hub, add wrist-view capture to any supported host without custom hardware fabrication.

To validate that EgoKit data can train robot policies, we replicated HumanEgo with 41 demonstrations recorded by EgoKit-PICO: in simulation, policies trained on 20 or 40 of them placed a cube on a tray in 60-74% of 100 unseen layouts, about as often as policies trained on Project Aria recordings of the same layouts.

EgoKit is available at https://egokit.chuange.org/.

summary.en: The paper presents EgoKit, a toolkit offering a shared egocentric recording workflow across six heterogeneous host devices, with locally stored video and a uniform log format. On XR headsets it also records head pose and OpenXR-standard 26-joint hand tracking aligned with video. Accessories enable wrist-view capture without custom hardware fabrication. To assess policy training, the authors replicated HumanEgo using 41 EgoKit-PICO demonstrations. In simulation, policies trained on 20 or 40 demonstrations placed a cube on a tray in 60–74% of 100 unseen layouts, about as often as policies trained on Project Aria recordings.
summary.zh: 论文提出 EgoKit，旨在让六种异构设备使用统一的第一人称数据录制流程，并生成本地视频和统一日志；XR 头显还记录与视频对齐的头部姿态及 OpenXR 标准 26 关节手部追踪。配套腕部相机、头带和 USB-C 集线器无需定制硬件即可增加腕部视角。作者以 EgoKit-PICO 录制的 41 段示范复现 HumanEgo：仿真中，使用其中 20 或 40 段训练的策略，在 100 种未见布局中有 60%–74% 将方块放到托盘上，表现约与使用相同布局的 Project Aria 录制数据训练的策略相当。

items.title: EgoKit: Towards Unified Low-Cost Egocentric Data Collection with Heterogeneous Devices

sections.text:
Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal).Yet existing simulators idealize these sensors, hiding critical modality-specific failure modes that limit real-world deployment.

We present VisionSIM, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities.

We expose fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters, reproducing failure modes overlooked by general-purpose simulators: pileup and glare for LiDAR; phase wrapping, saturation, and motion artifacts for iToF; refractory drops for event cameras; and history-dependent emission for thermal cameras.

This enables principled cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. We release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground-truth annotations.

summary.en: The paper presents VisionSIM, a physically grounded simulator for robotic perception across conventional and emerging sensor modalities. It models raw measurement processes and exposes physical sensor parameters to reproduce failure modes such as LiDAR pileup and glare, iToF phase wrapping and motion artifacts, event-camera refractory drops, and history-dependent thermal emission. The authors say the platform supports cross-modality comparisons on identical scenes and trajectories, and release an indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and ground-truth annotations.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 VisionSIM，一个面向机器人感知的多模态物理仿真平台。它模拟相机、事件、SPAD、iToF/dToF 和热成像等传感器的原始测量过程，并支持细粒度物理参数控制，以呈现通用模拟器可能忽略的失效模式，包括激光雷达的堆积与眩光、iToF 的相位缠绕与运动伪影、事件相机的折返丢失以及热相机的历史相关发射。作者称该平台可在相同场景和轨迹上比较不同模态，并发布了含同步原始测量与标注的室内数据集。

items.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception

Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). sections.text:
Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE).

These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent.

As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria?

We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions.

More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.

summary.en: The paper examines whether exposing embodied agents to benchmark success criteria improves task performance or encourages overfitting to the verifier. The authors note that criteria may demand more than the language instructions, making scores an imperfect measure of task completion. In controlled experiments, exposure increased code success under the given criteria, but the advantage vanished after slight criterion changes, and learned skills transferred poorly across tasks. The paper proposes instruction-faithful criteria and reports that they better reflect agent-generated program performance.
summary.zh: 论文研究具身自我改进中向智能体公开基准验证标准的影响。作者指出，这些标准可能比语言指令要求更多，因此得分未必准确反映任务是否完成。受控实验显示，公开标准后，智能体生成的代码在原标准下成功率更高，但标准略有变化时优势消失，且学到的技能跨任务迁移较差。作者还提出更忠于指令的验证标准，并称其更能反映智能体生成程序的表现。

items.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated.

For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios.

We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations.

We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions.

We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.

summary.en: The paper presents OopsieRecover, a framework for learning transferable recovery behaviors for vision-language-action models from a small number of corrective demonstrations. It uses abduction to infer the demonstrations’ intent and encodes that knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs that steer actions away from undesirable regions. Experiments across six tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks indicate that a handful of demonstrations can support recovery in novel situations without collecting new corrective data for each variation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 OopsieRecover，用少量语义干预示范帮助视觉-语言-动作模型从操作失败中恢复，并将纠正方法迁移到新情境。该框架通过溯因推断示范背后的意图，再把知识编码为稠密空间表示和条件代价，引导策略避开不理想行为区域。作者在六项任务及物体姿态、场景和相关任务变化中进行实验，报告少量纠正示范即可帮助模型应对多种新情境，无需为每种变化重新收集纠正数据。

items.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions

sections.text:
Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) lets robots search for run-time object queries, but fixed-rate inference spends embedded compute on low-value frames during idle motion, map revisits, or stable viewpoints. This paper presents an energy-aware OVD scheduler for low-power mobile robots.

The scheduler uses odometry, map change, and detector confidence to switch among low-, mid-, and high-power YOLO-World-S modes on a Jetson Orin Nano. We evaluate the energy-quality trade-off on an AgileX LIMO using 40 real navigation trials: two target objects, five placements per target-policy pair, and four perception policies.

Across bottle and cup trials, the scheduler records 8/10 mission success compared with 7/10 for each fixed-rate baseline, while reducing mean Jetson input power (a Jetson-side power-draw metric) by 5.2% relative to an 8 Hz high-rate baseline and lowering achieved OVD call rate by 34.0%.

It does not minimize mission-window Jetson input energy because longer missions can erase instantaneous power savings. A separate 60 s stationary microbenchmark isolates the perception workload: the scheduler lowers mean power from 8.045 W to 7.301 W and energy from 484.7 J to 438.1 J relative to the 8 Hz baseline.

These results support robot-state-aware OVD scheduling as a promising power-management mechanism with competitive task reliability, while showing that mission-window Jetson input energy must be read together with task progress and runtime.

summary.en: The paper introduces an energy-aware scheduler for open-vocabulary detection on low-power mobile robots. It switches among YOLO-World-S power modes using odometry, map changes, and detector confidence. In 40 real navigation trials on an AgileX LIMO, it achieved 8/10 mission successes across bottle and cup trials, versus 7/10 for each fixed-rate baseline, while reducing mean Jetson input power and detector call rate relative to the 8 Hz baseline. It did not reduce mission-window input energy; a separate 60-second stationary benchmark showed lower power and energy. The authors emphasize interpreting energy alongside task progress and runtime.
summary.zh: 论文提出面向低功耗移动机器人的开放词汇检测调度器，依据里程计、地图变化和检测置信度，在不同功耗的 YOLO-World-S 模式间切换。作者在 AgileX LIMO 上开展 40 次真实导航试验；瓶子与杯子任务中，调度器完成 8/10 次任务，固定频率基线各为 7/10，并相较 8 Hz 基线降低 Jetson 输入平均功率和检测调用率。它没有降低任务窗口内的 Jetson 输入能量；另一个 60 秒静止微基准显示，其功率和能量均低于该基线。作者认为评估能耗时需结合任务进展与运行时间。

items.title: Energy-Aware Open-Vocabulary Detection Scheduling for Low-Power Robotic Autonomy
